title: Hybrid continuous batcher memory-fragmentation study and scheduler knobs for mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our continuous batcher is seeing increased GPU memory fragmentation and KV-cache pressure on mixed prompt/response length traffic (short prompts with long responses and long prompts with short responses). This increases per-request latency variance and forces conservative slot reservations that lower throughput. Goal: identify scheduler knobs and allocator strategies that reduce fragmentation and eviction churn while keeping latency SLOs for both short-tail and long-tail workloads.

Scope: microbenchmarks + controlled canary that focus on: 
- slot packing policies for mixed-length slots (coalescing short tails behind long tokens)
- soft reservations for long-response sequences to prevent head-of-line blocking
- KV-cache slab sizing and compaction heuristics based on sequence-length histograms
- GPU allocator tuning to reduce fragmentation (slab compaction, deferred free, and lifetime-aware placement)

Non-goals: model architecture changes, network-level batching outside runtime, or customer-facing API changes in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: p50 and p95 token latency for mixed workloads improves or stays within +/-5% of baseline while throughput (tokens/sec) increases by >=8% on average in bench cluster
KV-cache eviction rate decreases by >=15% on the mixed-length experiment compared to current default policy
GPU memory fragmentation metric (percent unusable free memory) reduced by >=20% in the bench run
Observability: new telemetry charts show per-batcher-slot occupancy, eviction_count_by_seq_length_bin, and compaction_events, and those dashboards are linked in the ticket
A controlled canary plan is documented and a rollback path exists (canary to 5% traffic, monitor for increased tail latency or OOMs for 30 minutes)
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy bench runtime configured with mixed-length traffic generator (short prompt=16, long prompt=1024, response targets=16/1024 with 60/40 split). 2) Run baseline with current scheduler knobs (no soft reservations, default KV-slab) for 1 hour. 3) Enable hybrid slot coalescing and adaptive KV-slab compaction; run for 1 hour. 4) Collect telemetry: slot occupancy histograms, eviction_by_length, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU free fragmentation metric. 5) Compare runs using bench analysis notebook linked below.
experiment_plan: Matrix testing across three axes: (A) slot packing modes {strict, coalesce-short-behind-long, tail-priority}, (B) KV-slab policies {fixed-slab, adaptive-slab-by-length, aggressive-compaction}, (C) allocator behaviors {immediate-free, deferred-free-with-compaction, lifetime-aware-placement}. Each combination run for 1 hour in bench cluster with identical traffic. Primary comparisons are coalesce-short-behind-long + adaptive-slab + deferred-free vs baseline. We will run 3 warmup runs and 5 measurement runs per cell to account for noise. Results stored in s3 bucket: s3://redwood-bench/eng/ENG-40512/
rollout_plan: 1) Merge change behind feature flag. 2) Canary to 5% of traffic for 1 hour with elevated telemetry retention. 3) If metrics stable (no >10% regression p95 or >2x OOMs), extend to 25% for 4 hours. 4) Full rollout with gradual ramp and scheduled post-rollout review. Rollback: flip feature flag off; fallback route to quantized smaller model for impacted customers if necessary.
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggressive compaction may increase CPU usage and transient latency. Mitigation: limit compaction concurrency and run during low-traffic windows; experiment with incremental compaction windows.
Risk: new allocator behavior could surface rare OOMs. Mitigation: enable per-pod memory headroom buffer and OOM circuit breaker; canary at low percent and monitor OOM events closely.
Risk: telemetry may not capture subtle fragmentation patterns. Mitigation: add heap- and GPU-free-snapshot sampling at 10s intervals during experiments.
Risk: regression for single-tenant high-priority workloads. Mitigation: whitelist critical customers from the canary and run tenant-specific validations before rollout.
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike showing increased fragmentation on prod-mirrors. Attached initial heap snapshots and latency traces.
2025-02-18 Marco Ruiz: Completed initial microbench harness and captured baseline runs. Observed 28% unusable GPU free during mixed workload; KV eviction focused on mid-length sequences (128-512).

2025-02-24 Triage note: Decide to prioritize coalescing short requests behind long tails and an adaptive KV-slab size based on 24h seq-length histogram rather than per-minute adaptation to reduce churn.

2025-03-01 Marco Ruiz: Initial implementation of tail-aware coalescing behind feature flag. Bench results show tokens/sec +9% and p95 token latency -4% in coalescing mode with deferred-free allocator. Pushing PR for internal review.
2025-03-05 QA: Added dashboard links and smoke checks. Preparing canary plan for 5% traffic next week.
